# Planner evaluation (generated by scripts/planner_eval.py; do not edit by hand)

Test split, 610 of 744 images with at least 5 ground-truth tiles (6x8 grid, YOLO11m detections at confidence 0.10 and above, transformer trained on the val split only).

Selection rule: take the K highest-scoring tiles of each image (ties broken by a fixed seeded noise). Priority of a tile = sum of the class weights of the ground-truth boxes whose centre falls in it (same weights as the heuristic planner). Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over images (2000 resamples).

## 1. How much ground-truth priority do the selected tiles capture?

Priority captured = priority in the K selected tiles divided by the priority in the best possible K tiles (1.000 is perfect).

## 2. Route over the selected tiles: optimised route vs serpentine sweep

Both routes visit exactly the same K tiles, start at the entry tile (0,0) and are measured in tile units (not metres or minutes). Optimised = nearest neighbour followed by 2-opt (the dashboard planner). Serpentine = row-by-row sweep restricted to those tiles.

| K | method | optimised length | serpentine length | serpentine minus optimised (mean [95% CI]) | optimised shorter / equal / longer (% of images) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | oracle (ground-truth priority) | 7.68 | 9.51 | 1.83 [1.67, 1.99] | 66.7 / 33.1 / 0.2 |
| 3 | random | 9.10 | 10.56 | 1.46 [1.31, 1.61] | 58.2 / 41.3 / 0.5 |
| 3 | heuristic (class weight x confidence) | 8.13 | 9.81 | 1.68 [1.52, 1.83] | 65.1 / 34.6 / 0.3 |
| 3 | learned (transformer) | 7.64 | 9.45 | 1.82 [1.65, 1.98] | 66.9 / 33.0 / 0.2 |
| 5 | oracle (ground-truth priority) | 10.05 | 13.68 | 3.63 [3.40, 3.88] | 86.1 / 13.6 / 0.3 |
| 5 | random | 12.27 | 15.63 | 3.35 [3.12, 3.60] | 83.4 / 15.1 / 1.5 |
| 5 | heuristic (class weight x confidence) | 10.73 | 14.35 | 3.62 [3.39, 3.88] | 87.7 / 11.5 / 0.8 |
| 5 | learned (transformer) | 10.05 | 13.63 | 3.59 [3.36, 3.83] | 88.2 / 11.6 / 0.2 |
| 8 | oracle (ground-truth priority) | 13.68 | 19.48 | 5.80 [5.51, 6.11] | 95.6 / 3.8 / 0.7 |
| 8 | random | 15.98 | 22.80 | 6.81 [6.49, 7.16] | 97.9 / 1.5 / 0.7 |
| 8 | heuristic (class weight x confidence) | 14.36 | 20.38 | 6.02 [5.73, 6.33] | 96.6 / 3.0 / 0.5 |
| 8 | learned (transformer) | 13.48 | 19.18 | 5.69 [5.42, 5.97] | 95.1 / 3.6 / 1.3 |

In every row the 95% interval of (serpentine minus optimised) is above 0, so the optimised route is shorter on average.
The optimised route is not guaranteed to beat the serpentine on every image (2-opt starts from a nearest-neighbour tour); the last column shows how often it does.

## 4. Limitations

- Priority comes from ground-truth boxes weighted by assumed class weights, so this measures how well the planner finds the tiles that matter under that definition, not real cleanup effort.
- Route lengths are in tile units from a fixed entry tile; they say nothing about walking time, terrain or GPS.
- The transformer was trained on val-split detections and evaluated on test; the YOLO11m detector was trained on the train split. One training run of each.
- The comparison covers one fixed rule (top-K tiles). The dashboard threshold rule selects a different number of tiles per image and is not evaluated here.
